etymologies.etymologyHTML: From free +‎ way.

definitions.definition: (US, Parts of Canada and Australia) A highway with grade-separated crossings (rather than level crossings) and designed (and only permitted) for high-speed motor-traffic running in two directions on one separate carriageway each

quote.citation: 1983, David Brodsly, L. A. Freeway: An Appreciative Essay‎[1], page 1:
quote.text: Contrary to what one might expect of an essay on freeways, this one is neither a diatribe nor a paean.

quote.citation: 1999 June, “Transportation”, in A Brief Introduction to the Republic of China‎[2], Government Information Office, →ISBN, →OCLC, page 110:
quote.text: A 106-kilometer section of this 117-kilometer new freeway (between Hsinchu and Hsichih 汐止) was opened to traffic in 1997, and the entire line will be finished in December 1999.

quote.citation: 2008, Derek Hayes, Canada: An Illustrated History‎[3], page 257:
quote.text: In the late 1950s and 1960s most large cities started planning freeway systems, acknowledging the incredible growth in car ownership.

quote.citation: 2010, Robert Freestone, Urban Nation: Australia′s Planning Heritage‎[4], page 161:
quote.text: The Australian freeway story of the late twentieth century, like many planning stories, can be told as one of high technical expectations dashed by political controversy.

Synonyms: and some parts of North America) expressway
(If part of the Interstate Highway System) interstate

Antonyms: in order to avoid confusion with a toll road which often is referred to as freeway.) tollway
